Royals Have Long Loved the Cotswolds. Now Americans Do, Too.
 
Plus, the Frank Lloyd Wright of the South, and Thierry Henry lists his New York penthouse
 
By Candace Taylor
 
 
Naunton Village in the Cotswolds. GETTY IMAGES/ISTOCKPHOTO
 

This is an edition of the WSJ Homes newsletter, a weekly guide to luxurious properties, celebrity homes, interior design and the housing market. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

The presence of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle in the English countryside has caused a furor in recent weeks. But if Meghan ends up buying a home in the Cotswolds or nearby “Notswolds,” she’ll be far from the first American to do so. The idyllic rural region—think stone walls, green pastures and palatial estates—has recently become trendy with U.S. buyers, including Ellen DeGeneres and Portia De Rossi. One Cotswolds real-estate agent estimated that he has seen a 25% increase in U.S. buyers since last summer. As an avowed “Downton Abbey” fan, I wish I could join them.

 

We look at three key housing markets in the area: There’s the glamorous “Hollywood” Cotswolds, where denizens include Ellen and Portia, the Beckhams and Kate Moss. In the low-key “Royal-Friendly” Cotswolds, King Charles and Princess Anne have country homes. And in the up-and-coming “Notswolds” region nearby—where Princess Diana spent her teenage years—buyers can get the same rolling countryside and beautiful villages, but at a lower pricepoint.

 

Closer to home, we looked at the architecture of E. Fay Jones, a protégé of Frank Lloyd Wright who practiced primarily in Arkansas. In recent years, the visibility of Jones houses has risen and they can now fetch over $1 million—far above the median listing price in the area.

 

Meanwhile, this was a big week for celebrity real estate. Mansion had exclusive reporting on deals involving Angelina Jolie, Meg Ryan and French soccer legend Thierry Henry.

 
 
 

Cotswolds or ‘Notswolds’?

 
 
This ten-bedroom manor house in the Gloucestershire Cotswolds is one the market for about $8 million. SAVILLS
 

The Cotswolds, a famed stretch of English countryside, is drawing a growing number of American buyers. The Cotswolds—and increasingly, the up-and-coming Notswolds—are attractive to buyers for their rolling hills, picturesque villages and proximity to London.

A Hamptons Home for Less than $1 Million

 
 
MEDIA HAMPTONS
 

In the third installment of our series on the challenge of building an architect-designed, custom home for less than $1 million, we look at the Hamptons property of Charles Tesler. In one of the most expensive housing markets in the country, he managed to stay on budget by turning to modular construction.

 
 
 

What’s the Deal?

 
 
CEDRIC RIBEIRO/GETTY IMAGES
 

French soccer legend Thierry Henry and his partner, Andrea Rajacic, are listing their Manhattan penthouse for $25 million after relocating to Europe. The home has a private rooftop with a pergola and barbecue area.

 

Oscar-winning actress Angelina Jolie has sold her Los Angeles estate for $24.75 million, slightly more than what she paid in 2017. The star purchased the Los Feliz estate for about $24.5 million in 2017, after filing for divorce from Brad Pitt.

 

“When Harry Met Sally….” actress Meg Ryan has sold her Hamptons home for $15.25 million to Broadway producer Henry Tisch, a member of the prominent Tisch family.
